why: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at plugins/marketplace-reference.md#entry-and-plugin-json (was line 195 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (whole line read; single sentence after a one-clause preamble, no reversal). The IDENTIFIER claim is also accurate: MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS (external-catalog-adapters.ts:153) carries the 7 path fields plus displayName/description/version/author/homepage/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -a` returns zero for category/tags/relevance/license/keywords in that file. The finding is refuted on its CONSEQUENCE, on four independent grounds. (1) It is a deliberate, reasoned, TESTED decision, not an oversight. The allowlist's own docblock at :141-152 states it: 'Deliberately an ALLOWLIST, not a copy of the entry: a catalog row is untrusted input from a repository the user may not control, and a key no adapter reads has no business travelling through the install record onto disk. The metadata half is the subset the Claude adapter actually consumes (normalizeClaudePluginBundle).' A committed regression test pins it: marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:406-431 places `relevance: { keywords: ['review'] }` on an entry under the comment 'Not a field any adapter reads - must not travel with the definition' and asserts fields keys equal ['description','mcpServers','skills','version']. The finding's own example field is the one the test names. (2) WRONG LAYER - the stated consequence is unreachable from the cited line. `fields` is a MANIFEST OVERLAY consumed by the format adapter, not the browse-row source. The Discover row is MarketplaceCatalogItem (marketplace/types.ts:340-400), built by proposalToCatalogItem (registry-catalog-items.ts) from entryDescription/entryVersion/capabilities/source - and that interface has no category/tags/keywords member at all. Carrying `category` into `fields` would put it in a manifest overlay whose target type, NessyPluginManifest (plugins/types.ts:715-758), also has no category/tags/license/keywords/repository. (3) NOT MARKETPLACE-ENTRY-SPECIFIC - our plugin.json reader drops exactly the same fields: schema.ts:501-525 rebuilds the manifest copying only description/publisher/homepageUrl/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -c -a license` returns 0 in format-adapters/claude.ts, plugins/schema.ts and plugins/types.ts. So this is a uniform 'we do not model informational metadata' property applied identically to plugin.json and to a marketplace entry, not a divergence at the catalog parse. (4) NO DOCUMENTED BEHAVIOUR IS MISSED, and the drop is not a rejection. The quoted sentence establishes only that an entry MAY carry these fields; the doc tables gloss them as 'Plugin category for organization' / 'Tags for searchability' / 'Discovery tags' and no page in the Claude Code corpus (plugin-marketplaces.md, discover-plugins.md, plugins.md, plugins-reference.md) documents Claude Code reading, rendering or filtering by category, tags or keywords. plugins/manifest-reference.md#unrecognized-fields (was lines 470-471 of the retired plugins-reference page) states the opposite posture verbatim: 'Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize. You can keep metadata from another ecosystem in plugin.json and the plugin still loads.' Our parser does the same - ExternalPluginCatalogPluginDto has an index signature, unknown keys emit no diagnostic and the entry still resolves and installs. Finally the 'Discover list' phrasing names a SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: Nessy's Discover shelves group per-registry (MarketplaceBrowsePage sections keyed by marketplaceRegistryId), and the tag/tenant/profession facet vocabulary that does exist belongs to the corporate Skills Market API (marketplace/client.ts:123-133,185-188), a different data source from a Claude marketplace.json - so there is no category axis for an external catalog to lose. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; those are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) - but it is the same class: a decision with a written reason and a guarding test. Separately: `relevance` is already tracked on its own as coverage-map row 60 (plugin-relevance, red), so folding it into this row double-counts a registered gap; and that row's note ('relevance passes inside the marketplace entry fields') is contradicted by the test above and should be corrected to 'dropped at parse'.
correctedState: MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS (packages/shared/src/marketplace/external-catalog-adapters.ts:153) is a deliberate security allowlist, documented at :141-152 and pinned by a regression test at marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:406-431. It carries exactly the keys the format adapter can act on. category, tags, relevance, license, keywords and repository are IGNORED, never rejected: the entry still parses, resolves its source and installs, which matches plugins/manifest-reference.md#unrecognized-fields (was line 470 of the retired plugins-reference page) ('Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize'). The omission is not marketplace-entry-specific - NessyPluginManifest (plugins/types.ts:715-758) and our plugin.json reader (plugins/schema.ts:501-525) model none of these fields either. The claimed Discover-list consequence is unreachable from this line: the browse row MarketplaceCatalogItem (marketplace/types.ts:340-400) has no category/tags member and Discover shelves group by registry, not by entry category; the tag facets that exist belong to the separate corporate Skills Market API (marketplace/client.ts:123-133). If a category/tag browse axis for external catalogs is wanted, that is a new product feature spanning MarketplaceCatalogItem and the browse UI, not a parser fix - and it is undocumented in Claude's corpus. The one genuinely open sub-item, relevance, is already tracked as coverage-map row 60 (plugin-relevance).
